newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch closing share market report.
newsitem.headline: Dutch closing share market report.

text.p: Dutch shares drifted down from Wednesday's record close in light profit-taking, but financials caught the eye with moderate gains for banks ABN AMRO and ING.
The AEX index closed down 0.32 points at 581.59, slipping just 0.05 percent from their all-time high.
ING Bank was the most traded stock, with a sizeable turnover of 6.6 million shares. Both it and ABN AMRO were up 70 cents, ING to 54.70 guilders, ABN to 97.50.
Some traders said the inflated trading was the result of speculation that ING was interested in buying Swiss insurer Winterthur, a rumour on which the bank refused to comment.
"We've seen quite a lot of demand (for the stock) in the U.S. and their results are expected to be good," one trader said.

Koninklijke PTT Nederland (KPN) was typical of a number of early week risers, dipping 50 cents to close at 60.10 guilders. The shares rose 1.70 on Wednesday after the announcement of a takeover bid for TNT of Australia.
"It was up sharply on Wednesday. Profit-taking has brought it back today," one trader said.
